name: Semaglutide
used_for: FDA-labeled for chronic weight management and reducing cardiovascular risk in adults with obesity or overweight (Wegovy), MASH with liver fibrosis (Wegovy, accelerated approval), and type 2 diabetes glycemic control, cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction (Ozempic), each alongside diet and activity changes where specified.

entries.text: Wegovy injection: labeled starting dose 0.25 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 4 weeks, with stepwise increases every 4 weeks (0.5 mg, 1 mg, 1.7 mg) toward a maintenance dose that varies by indication (labeled maintenance typically 1.7 to 2.4 mg weekly; label also describes up to 7.2 mg weekly for weight reduction).
entries.population: Adults (and pediatric patients 12 years and older for weight reduction) per the Wegovy label

entries.text: Wegovy tablets: labeled starting dose 1.5 mg orally once daily for 30 days, then 4 mg, then 9 mg in 30-day steps, with a maintenance dose of 25 mg daily.
entries.population: Adults with obesity or overweight per the Wegovy label

entries.text: Ozempic injection: labeled starting dose 0.25 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg weekly, with optional increases to 1 mg and then 2 mg weekly (maximum) after at least 4 weeks at each dose.
entries.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes per the Ozempic label

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Wegovy (semaglutide) injection and tablets, revised June 2026.
research.finding: Lists approved uses for weight reduction, cardiovascular risk reduction, and MASH, with a dose-escalation schedule.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Ozempic (semaglutide) injection.
research.finding: Lists approved uses in adults with type 2 diabetes: glycemic control, cardiovascular risk reduction, and kidney outcomes, with escalation up to 2 mg weekly.

research.summary: STEP 1: randomized, double-blind trial of semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly versus placebo for 68 weeks in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes (Wilding et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: Average weight change was -14.9% with semaglutide versus -2.4% with placebo; nausea and diarrhea were the most common side effects.

research.summary: SUSTAIN-6: randomized trial of once-weekly semaglutide versus placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk (Marso et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: Major cardiovascular events occurred in 6.6% with semaglutide versus 8.9% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.74); retinopathy complications were more frequent with semaglutide.
